data.name: Libra of the Vampire Princess: Lycoris & Aoi in "The Promise" PLUS Iris in "Homeworld"
data.detailed_description:
These episodes take place BEFORE "Libra of the Vampire Princess", so they're a great introduction into Libra's vampire world. They're also perfect for fans who crave more of Libra's expanded universe. Both episodes were funded on Kickstarter thanks to our amazing Backers.

Libra of the Vampire Princess: Lycoris & Aoi in "The Promise"


“We promised each other, Aoi, that we wouldn’t die alone.” -Lycoris

Lycoris wasn’t always a dim-witted, scythe-swinging servant of darkness; she was a well-known agent in the Rubina: a holy organization of skilled monster fighters and vampire slayers. In this narrative, we go back in time and explore the circumstances of how her and Aoi came to be formally paired together as “buddies” in the Rubina. On a deeper level, we hone in on a particularly gruesome event that would come to shape their eternal love and respect for one another—a bond which can never be broken.

With moments of comedy, drama, and gory combat, Lycoris and Aoi’s episode is a must play, especially if you're a fan of this sweet duo.

Libra of the Vampire Princess Extra: Iris in "Homeworld"


Dernière, one of the many worlds that exist in different dimensions. As holders of a special power known as "life force", Dernièreans were blessed with vast energy and extended lifespans, and they lived in glorious prosperity. However, even for them the day of ruin approaches.

Taking place thousands of years before the events chronicled in Libra of the Vampire Princess, catch a glimpse Dernière’s tragic history and the lives of those caught in the middle. You will meet Aconite Embroche, the determined leader of the Bebel’s sixth commando unit, and his smitten lieutenant, Iris Pumila. Together with Galega Officinalis, a lecherous and gifted dollmaker, they use their superhuman powers to combat the infected life force from spreading and consuming their homeworld.

With moments of comedy, explosive battle scenes, and sexiness, this episode is a must play especially if you're an Iris fan!

Playtime: 5 hours

reviews.review:
First of all, I’d like to point the fact that this kinetic (there are no choices, you only read) visual novel is [b]very expensive[/b] for such little content¹. I still haven’t played the original game, and I bought this title since in the description it says that it’s a good introduction of the world of [i]Libra of the Vampire Princess[/i]. I’m very interested on that game, but since it’s expensive as well, I’ll wait for a sale. 

This title consists in two short episodes: two girls called Lycoris and Aoi who are agents of an organization called Rubina. The girls dress as nuns and they kill vampires, in order to protect innocent people. [spoiler]Aoi is kinda of an a.s.s to Lycoris sometimes, trying to prove herself by saying some disrespectful things about Lycoris’ late partners.[/spoiler] Then there’s a few semi romantic scenes and dialogue between them, both characters insist that they love each other, but “not like that”. There’s some fanservice because of it, which I liked. The ending was pretty abrupt tho, things were getting cute and it ended faster before I could even say “Aww—“. lol

The second story is very different, some sort of sci-fi mixed with an occult group trying to take over the power. A woman called Iris together with her colleagues, Aconite and Galega [spoiler](he’s weird as f*ck but I liked him?? He has a fetish for Iris’ legs because he thinks they’re perfect but it’s not like he loves her. Just… her legs. lol[/spoiler], take down these crazy guys that are part of the occult group that want people to get infected with an impure life force. Wow. [spoiler]And it ends up being something totally different.[/spoiler]

5/10. The art style together with BGM and VA are pretty good, but honestly, the price tag bothers me a lot. Lycoris and Aoi’s story where a good introduction to the original game (at least you get to know a bit of the plot), and Iris route was basically for fanservice. Which is fine, but just… If you haven’t played the original game yet, how can this second story be considered a “good introduction to the original”? Even so, it was fun. The ending was unexpected at least. Overall, I recommend to get this title AFTER you read Libra of the Vampire Princess, and only if you liked the story a lot in order to pay an absurd amount of money on two short kinetic novels. You can always wait for a good sale too, it’s up to you.

[b]¹ There’s an achievement that requires 10 hours of gameplay. So I let it idle in order to get it. I finished the whole game in 2 hours or less.[/b]
